name: Srikanth Iyer
headline: How do simple parts reach one shared decision?
shortBio: I study collective intelligence: how groups of simple agents, with no leader and no view of the whole, still reach a shared decision, and why some of those decisions survive a noisy world.
bio: I'm a PhD researcher in Systems Science at Binghamton University's CASCI lab, and a Research Fellow in the CBeRa group at the Católica Biomedical Research Centre in Lisbon. I work with cellular automata, Boolean networks, genetic algorithms and, lately, language-model agents.

Before research I spent fifteen years in media: sports writing, commercials, event films and screenplays, including co-writing the feature film Capgras and developing series for BBC Studios India. I still think in stories, which is why my research comes with pictures.
